items.title: Investment context anchors the corporate-learning boundary
items.summary: Vortex describes its November 2016 investment with henQ and an integrated corporate learning offer.
items.implication: Model a durable employer learning domain; use current product sources for today's capability scope.

items.title: Skills work needs role definitions and evidence
items.summary: Skill Navigator describes role maps, skill levels and self, manager and 360-degree review.
items.implication: Proposed design: version requirements and preserve assessment provenance so gap closure has an interpretable denominator.

items.title: Learning impact extends beyond attendance
items.summary: The skills product page distinguishes progression and application from attendance and satisfaction.
items.implication: Proposed strategy: measure work application and skill reassessment alongside participation; do not claim causal productivity gains from correlation.

items.title: Learner relevance and employer presentation are connected
items.summary: The LXP page describes tailored discovery, personal learning views and branded academies.
items.implication: Proposed design: preserve accessible launch and resume paths while exposing why an intervention fits the learner's goal.

items.title: Qualifications have a lifecycle
items.summary: The LMS page lists recurring validity, renewal dates and exemption handling.
items.implication: Proposed design: explicit policy versions, evidence status and reviewed exceptions should determine readiness views.

items.title: Authoring acceleration requires maintained knowledge
items.summary: The authoring page describes uploaded source material, generated questions, co-authoring and versioning.
items.implication: Proposed design: retain source permissions and review provenance and provide a withdrawal path for superseded learning.

items.title: Events require operational capacity and evidence
items.summary: Event Management includes multiple cohorts, waitlists, reminders and attendance recording.
items.implication: Proposed design: distinguish registration, participation and completion, including cancellations and attendance corrections.

items.title: Content subscriptions and training bookings have different economics
items.summary: Studytube presents a proprietary library and e-learning subscriptions, while its support documentation separately describes DOI requests.
items.implication: Proposed design: separate content entitlement from a scheduled provider booking, its approval and its cancellation terms.

items.title: External training is an optional intermediary workflow
items.summary: Studytube support describes requesting and managing external training when the academy uses the DOI module.
items.implication: Proposed design: treat provider confirmation and employer approval as separate commitments; do not imply all courses run within the LMS.

items.title: Invoice handling depends on the customer arrangement
items.summary: Studytube's support material states that invoicing-service arrangements apply to some customers.
items.implication: Proposed design: select the contracted invoice route and reconcile booking references and credits; avoid assuming a universal merchant-of-record model.

items.title: Integration is part of the value proposition
items.summary: The integration page describes connections to HR, identity, learning content and BI, together with an API and LTI 1.3.
items.implication: Proposed design: authoritative workforce data stays in HR while the academy owns learning evidence; failed updates need reconciliation and replay.

items.title: Implementation spans more than tenant creation
items.summary: The implementation page describes handover, academy setup, migration, integrations and a transition to customer success.
items.implication: Proposed design: require an accountable pilot, reconciled migration and operational handover before broader adoption.

items.title: AI and data terms require explicit evaluation
items.summary: The legal-documentation page links separate processing, user and AI terms and security information.
items.implication: Proposed design: employer technical evaluation should establish approved processing scope and review access before enabling additional data uses.

items.title: Procurement improvement is a specific customer use case
items.summary: Studytube's a.s.r. case describes centralizing discovery and booking of external training.
items.implication: Proposed strategy: assess request-to-booking effort and reconciliation in a bounded employer pilot; do not generalize the case's reported savings.
